entities.summary: The Coomloughra Horseshoe is an exposed mountain circuit in County Kerry, Ireland, linking Beenkeragh, Carrauntoohil and Caher above a basin of mountain lakes.
entities.description: The Coomloughra Horseshoe starts at the Hydro car park near Glencar in County Kerry, Ireland. Climb clockwise through Skregmore to Beenkeragh, cross the rocky ridge to Carrauntoohil and return over Caher. Mountain lakes below and changing summit views reward the complete circuit. Allow a full mountain day: the narrow ridge requires climbing over steep rock using your hands, a head for heights and competent navigation. Choose settled, clear conditions; avoid wind or ice. The privately farmed Reeks prohibit dogs.
entities.whyWorthwhile: The Coomloughra Horseshoe in County Kerry links three high summits with rocky ridges and views into a lake-filled mountain basin. The sustained scenery makes the full circuit rewarding for experienced walkers comfortable climbing over exposed rock.

names.canonical: Mount Brandon via the Faha corrie

entities.summary: The Faha route climbs Mount Brandon in County Kerry, Ireland, through a hollow of mountain lakes and cliffs before returning the same way from the Atlantic-facing summit.
entities.description: Start the Mount Brandon walk at the small Faha car park outside Cloghane on Kerry’s Dingle Peninsula, Ireland. Pass the grotto, enter the lake-filled mountain hollow and climb the Éisc, a steep gully leading to the main ridge. Turn toward Mount Brandon’s summit and return the same way. The enclosed cliffs open into broad Atlantic views in clear weather. Allow around six hours and take particular care on the steep descent. Choose a favourable forecast and carry reliable navigation.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Mount Brandon’s Faha approach in County Kerry moves from lakes enclosed by cliffs to an open ridge above the Atlantic. That dramatic change of scenery rewards experienced walkers willing to tackle the steep ascent and descent.

entities.summary: Bunratty Castle and Folk Park in Ireland explores historical buildings, streets and domestic life in a substantial living-history setting.
entities.description: Bunratty Castle and Folk Park in Bunratty, Ireland, lets visitors explore historical buildings and streets as a setting for everyday life, rather than learning only from exhibit cases. That tangible environment gives it particular appeal for school-age children, teenagers and adults, with some appeal for preschool children. Check current operation and restrictions for individual activities before visiting.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Bunratty Castle and Folk Park in Ireland makes historical domestic life tangible through its buildings and streets.

entities.summary: EPIC in Dublin tells the story of Irish emigration through interactive digital displays that invite visitors to participate.

It is particularly suited to children aged nine and above, teenagers and adults. Check current operation and activity arrangements before visiting.
entities.whyWorthwhile: EPIC in Dublin is worth choosing for an actively participatory way to explore Irish emigration history.
